blurb:
Four months old and already has his whole life figured out. Liam is a domestic shorthair kitten who weighs about 5.7 pounds right now, which means he's still very much in the chaos phase of being a cat. He's litterbox trained already, which at four months is genuinely impressive and saves you the part of kitten ownership nobody talks about.

He gets along great with other cats, so if you've already got one at home, Liam would slot right in. He does best in a home without young kids, so he's ideal for adults or families with older children who know how to give a small animal some space while it settles in.

He's vaccinated, microchipped, flea treated, and neutered. Everything is already handled. Walk in during visiting hours and ask for Liam.

• Already litterbox trained at 4 months and fully vetted — lowest friction adoption in the batch

blurb:
Nobody knows exactly what a Boxer-Corgi mix is supposed to look like, but Asher figured it out. He's 40 pounds of ginger brindle, compact and goofy, and the volunteers at Mostly Mutts have been talking about him since he came in. He went through the Prison Pups immersive training program and learned a lot. He's four years old, in a foster home, and ready to go.

His foster calls him quirky and funny, and that tracks. He loves fetch and will bring the ball back every single time as long as you keep throwing it. He's also perfectly happy entertaining himself inside, and apparently makes an excellent desk dog. He'll just park himself under your chair and hang out while you work. Not bad for a home office setup.

He needs a house, not an apartment. He's vocal when he sees people outside and a backyard with a fence is going to make him much happier. He does best without other dogs or cats at home, and kids 15 and up are the right fit since younger kids and toddlers make him uncomfortable. His trainer will walk you through how to introduce him to other dogs, so his on-leash reactivity is very manageable.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. Visit their website to learn more about Asher and start the adoption inquiry.

blurb:
Cassie has been through the adoption process before. She found a family, settled in, and then life got complicated on their end. A new baby, a move, too much chaos. None of that was on her. She's seven years old, about 34 pounds, and a Beagle-Spaniel mix who just needs a home that's actually quiet enough for her to relax in.

She's sweet and affectionate once she feels safe. During her photo shoot she was friendly and calm the whole time. She's not bouncing off the walls. She's a mellow girl who does well with a routine and a patient family. If there's a man in the house, she'll warm up to him, she just needs him to take it slow with her at first.

She does best as an only dog at home, though she gets along fine with a neighbor dog who comes around for playdates. No cats, and younger kids are too much for her. If your house is calm and your kids are 15 or older, she's worth going to meet. She's in a foster home right now doing well, just waiting for the right fit.

Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw. You can browse her profile and reach out through their website to get the process started.

scoring_notes:

blurb:
Yasmeen is nine years old, about 62 pounds, and a Lab-Terrier mix who was pulled from animal control and put through the Mostly Mutts Prison Pups training program. Her foster mom says whoever adopts her is going to hit the jackpot. That's not fluff. Yasmeen earned it.

She came in a little unsure of people, which makes sense given where she started. But it only took one day in the training program for her to decide she trusted her people. Once she does, she's loyal and loving and wants to be close to you. She's got a protective side too. She'll let you know when a stranger comes around. That's the kind of dog some people are actually looking for.

She's done well with other dogs, including a Boxer she stayed with while her regular foster was on vacation. She warmed up to cats in her foster home, though every cat is different so that's worth a conversation. For kids, she liked the ones she met on a day trip and was giving out kisses, but because she showed some guarding behavior in one temporary home, her trainer recommends meeting her with dog-savvy kids 15 and up first.

If you want a calm, bonded senior dog who's going to take her job as your companion seriously, Yasmeen is the one to go meet. Reach out through mostlymutts.org to get started.

• Animal control origins plus senior age plus guarded placement criteria signal she has been in the system a long time and faces real adoption headwinds without a strong public push

blurb:
Gina came in as part of a litter with a Go-Gos theme, got adopted, and was returned a month later when she started having stomach issues. Several months of vet visits and food changes later, she's doing better, though she still vomits occasionally and nobody's figured out exactly why yet. Her foster, who has watched all of this unfold up close, calls her the best cat ever. That's worth paying attention to.

She's small, about five pounds, and will probably stay that way. She's playful and independent during the day, but she does love to snuggle when she wants to. She's lived happily with adult cats in her foster home and was completely unfazed when she met a dog on a leash, so she's adaptable in the right situation.

The stomach thing is real and worth knowing upfront. She's on a special diet, so if there are other cats in the home, you'd need a plan to feed her separately. It's manageable, it's just something to think through before you commit. If you've got the patience for a cat with a sensitive stomach and a foster mom singing her praises, Gina is worth a visit.

Reach out to Mostly Mutts through their website to submit an inquiry and set up a time to meet her.

blurb:
Twiggy had a home for several years before another cat joined the household and things went sideways. No drama, just two cats who didn't get along. She ended up back at Mostly Mutts, understandably rattled, and spent her first days at the shelter acting out a little. Her foster family gave her time to decompress, and the cat who showed up after that is a completely different story.

She chirps at guests. She stations herself by the front door when you get home. If she hasn't had enough attention, she'll make a few small cries until the situation is corrected. She's playful and curious and, once she's comfortable, genuinely friendly. She needs about a week to a week and a half to settle into a new space, but once she does, she relaxes into a low-maintenance, easygoing routine. She's not destructive and has never damaged anything in her foster home, though she does occasionally scratch at carpet, so a scratching post would go a long way.

She's best as an only cat, and probably happiest without a dog in the house either. Gentle kids are fine, but she'd want to meet them first. She's eight years old, which means she's done with the chaotic kitten phase and ready to just be someone's calm, loyal companion.

Submit an inquiry through Mostly Mutts' website to arrange a meet with Twiggy.

blurb:
She came into Mostly Mutts years ago as a nursing mom, raised her whole litter, watched them all get adopted, then found a home herself. That home didn't work out, and now she's back. Darby's been through a lot of transitions for a six-year-old cat, and she's still sweet as ever.

Her personality is pretty specific and pretty great. She follows her people around the house just to see what they're doing. She'll park herself on your lap for long stretches. She opens her mouth to meow but almost nothing comes out, which her adopters seem to find endearing. She also has extra toes, which is a genuinely fun thing to notice the first time you pick her up. When she's in a playful mood, she goes after balls and little fuzzy mice with full commitment.

She doesn't love being held, but she absolutely loves being near you. There's a difference, and she'll show you pretty quickly which one she's into. She's good with other cats and may do fine with gentle kids. Dogs are still an unknown. She's litter trained and keeps her space clean.

Mostly Mutts is a rescue based in Kennesaw. Head to their website to submit an adoption inquiry and set up a time to meet Darby in person.
